topic: Comprehensive handoff for the gen2/gen1 --version SIGSEGV residual (the 'third bug' documented in artifacts/audit/madaros_gen2_rodata_overflow_20260903.json, artifacts/audit/madaros_gen2_argslist_field_offset_20260903.json, and artifacts/audit/madaros_gen2_field_idx_crossstruct_leak_20260903.json, all part of PR #2408). Four independent fix attempts were implemented and verified against real gen1+gen2 self-compiles; NONE resolved the crash. This document records exactly what was tried, what was learned, and the most promising unexplored lead, so the next session does not repeat this work.
status: UNRESOLVED. No fix landed in the repository. All four fix attempts described below were reverted -- none is committed. The crash (gen2 --version, exit 139) is confirmed still present and byte-for-byte identical to the original signature across every attempt.

confirmed_facts_not_in_question.crash_mechanism: field_idx_for_base_ref, when compiling arg_list_get's body, resolves ArgList.len to field index 44 (the raw byte-hash fallback: ASCII 'l' = 108, 108 % 64 = 44) instead of the correct index 1. This was confirmed via print instrumentation printing the CURRENT function being lowered (cur_fn=arg_list_get) alongside the wrong result (typed_result=44), reproduced identically across every one of the ~10 separate instrumented builds performed across this investigation.
confirmed_facts_not_in_question.downstream_effect: The wrong field index (44, or 48 once native codegen adds native_v2_object_header_size()/8 = 4) makes arg_list_get read garbage as ArgList.len, so its `i >= lst.len` bounds check never trips; it then reads garbage from the similarly-miscomputed items[0] slot -- which happens to be the raw 8-byte ASCII content of the unrelated string literal "--output" -- and returns that as if it were a real string. compiler_mode_has_flag's `arg_list_get(args, i) == needle` then calls str_eq with that garbage as a pointer, which dereferences it and segfaults. This full chain was independently confirmed via gdb (runtime register/memory trace) AND via compile-time print instrumentation (two completely different techniques converging on the same explanation) -- see the two companion audit files.
confirmed_facts_not_in_question.exactly_5_wrong_calls_out_of_68: Across the whole main.sio self-compile, field_idx_for_base_ref is asked to resolve ArgList.len exactly 68 times (matching every ArgList.len access site across compiler_mode_has_flag, compiler_mode_option_string, get_args, arg_list_get, etc. -- each function that touches ArgList.len gets asked once per occurrence in its body). 63 of the 68 calls correctly resolve to 1; exactly 5 resolve to 44, and cur_fn=arg_list_get accounts for 2 of those 5 (the other 3 wrong calls belong to run_int_to_string_bench_from_args, run_probe_char_from_i64, and run_probe_arg_list_get -- i.e. OTHER functions that also touch ArgList.len are ALSO affected, not just arg_list_get, though only arg_list_get's corruption is reachable from --version's actual execution path and hence the one that crashes).

fix_attempts_tried_and_reverted.hypothesis: field_idx_from_name stops at the FIRST struct_layouts entry named 'ArgList' and, if the field isn't found there, falls straight into an untyped cross-struct scan rather than checking for a LATER, more-complete entry with the same name.
fix_attempts_tried_and_reverted.change: Modified field_idx_from_name (self-hosted/ir/lower.sio) to scan ALL entries named struct_name (tracking found_struct) before falling through to the cross-struct/hash fallback.
fix_attempts_tried_and_reverted.result: No effect. Crash signature byte-identical. This defensive change is plausibly still a real, independent hardening (the underlying risk it guards against -- a struct registered more than once with one incomplete copy -- is real and documented elsewhere in the same file), but it does not touch the actual bug: the wrong value doesn't come from a duplicate entry, it comes from struct_layouts never having a usable ArgList entry AT ALL by the time arg_list_get is compiled.

fix_attempts_tried_and_reverted.hypothesis: lowerer_lower_program_items_mut's single per-item loop registers a struct's fields (ItemStruct) and lowers function bodies (ItemFn) in the SAME pass, in item-list order -- so a function defined right after its own struct could have its body lowered before the struct's registration in THAT SAME pass runs.
fix_attempts_tried_and_reverted.change: Added a new pre-pass, lowerer_preregister_struct_fields_multipass_mut, called at the top of lowerer_lower_program_items_mut, registering every struct's complete fields (via the existing lowerer_register_struct_fields_direct_mut) before the main loop's body-lowering begins.
fix_attempts_tried_and_reverted.result: No effect. Crash signature byte-identical. Follow-up diagnostic instrumentation (print-tagging every known struct-field-registration call site) proved lowerer_lower_program_items_mut is not even the function that processes main.sio's items during a real `gen1.elf build main.sio out.elf` compile -- main.sio goes through a completely different, dedicated multi-module pipeline (module_frontend.sio's `imported_compile`, calling lower_dep_program_items_into_acc_with_externs). This whole function, and therefore this fix, is dead code for the failing scenario.

fix_attempts_tried_and_reverted.hypothesis: lowerer_preseed_external_items_into_acc_mut (part of the real multi-module pipeline, processing every OTHER module's items relative to whichever module is 'self' in a given pass) has an inline struct registration that SKIPS re-registering a struct name it has already seen, even if the earlier registration was incomplete (e.g. missing a field due to spec_dce_filter_with_global_marks pruning it from one program's restricted view).
fix_attempts_tried_and_reverted.change: Modified the skip-duplicate check to instead prefer whichever registration has MORE fields, replacing an incomplete earlier entry in place rather than leaving it stuck.
fix_attempts_tried_and_reverted.result: No effect on the crash, AND this attempt introduced a real, measured performance regression: the gen1->gen2 self-compile that normally takes ~40-70 minutes took over 2 hours with this change. Follow-up instrumentation confirmed the underlying premise was itself wrong: EVERY one of the 124 times this function processes ArgList, the AST-level field list it sees already has exactly 2 fields (raw_field_count=2, always) -- there is no incomplete copy to guard against here; the 'prefer longer' logic was solving a problem that does not occur at this call site. This is the attempt to actively AVOID re-trying -- it is a net-negative (slower, no benefit) and was fully reverted.

fix_attempts_tried_and_reverted.hypothesis: lowerer_preseed_program_items_mut (used to build the IrProgramSummary that seeds struct_layouts for the 'hot path' single-Lowerer body-lowering route, lower_program_bodies_from_summary_with_epistemic_boxed_owned <- lowerer_new_from_program_summary_owned, which takes struct_layouts directly from the summary) calls lowerer_register_struct_fields_direct_mut as a SEPARATE function call, passing &(*sd).fields -- the exact shape of reference-through-a-boxed-field argument that the codebase's OWN comments already document as silently no-op'ing when passed across a function-call boundary (see the identical, already-fixed issue at lowerer_preseed_external_struct_items_mut, whose comment reads: 'lowerer_register_struct_fields_mut silently no-ops from this call site (suspected lean_single handling of &(*box).field through FieldDefList head)').
fix_attempts_tried_and_reverted.change: Replaced the separate-function-call with an inline registration (mirroring the already-proven-correct workaround pattern used at lowerer_preseed_external_struct_items_mut and lowerer_preseed_external_items_into_acc_mut), avoiding the cross-function-boundary reference passing entirely.
fix_attempts_tried_and_reverted.result: No effect. Crash signature byte-identical. Follow-up diagnostic instrumentation placed INSIDE the new inline code, gated on the struct name being 'ArgList', printed ZERO times across the entire gen2 self-compile -- meaning lowerer_preseed_program_items_mut's ItemStruct branch is NEVER REACHED for ArgList at all during this compile. The hypothesis about WHICH function builds the relevant IrProgramSummary was itself wrong, or this function is reached for OTHER modules/structs but not for whichever module/pass ultimately compiles arg_list_get.

the_core_unresolved_question: Given exhaustive print-instrumentation of every one of the ~9 known struct_layouts-writing call sites in self-hosted/ir/lower.sio (see the list below), NONE could be shown, with certainty, to be the one that determines the wrong (or even the right) field index seen by arg_list_get specifically. Some sites (lowerer_preseed_external_items_into_acc_mut / 'site_fix3', lowerer_preseed_external_struct_items_mut / 'site6' when checked with a RELIABLE ir_name_eq-based marker rather than a naive byte-comparison) DO fire for ArgList, correctly, with the right field count (2) every time -- yet the wrong value (44) STILL appears for arg_list_get specifically, in exactly 2 of its accesses. This means either: (a) there is a TENTH, still-unfound call site or code path that ALSO writes an incomplete/wrong ArgList entry AFTER the correct ones have already run (a last-write-wins clobber), or (b) the Lowerer instance that eventually compiles arg_list_get's body is a DIFFERENT, disconnected struct_layouts table from whichever one(s) my markers observed firing correctly -- i.e. the correlation between 'registration happened' and 'the compiling Lowerer sees it' is broken somewhere in this fast-summary/multi-module machinery, in a way that was not pinned down before time ran out on this investigation.

all_registration_call_sites_checked.site: lowerer_register_struct_fields_direct_mut (self-hosted/ir/lower.sio ~3037, shared function, 4 call sites: main.sio's original struct-decl loop x3 plus this session's attempt-2 pre-pass)
all_registration_call_sites_checked.reliable_marker_result: ZERO hits for ArgList across every build that included this marker, despite being called (per source) from contexts that should reach ArgList's declaration. Never definitively explained -- either never actually called for ArgList, or the CALL ITSELF silently no-ops (matching the exact bug class already documented elsewhere in this file for the sibling _mut function) before reaching the print statement at the top of the callee.

all_registration_call_sites_checked.site: lowerer_register_struct_fields_mut (self-hosted/ir/lower.sio ~3095, the append-based sibling, 1 call site inside lowerer_lower_program_items_mut's main loop)
all_registration_call_sites_checked.reliable_marker_result: ZERO hits. Consistent with lowerer_lower_program_items_mut not being the active pipeline for this compile (confirmed separately).

all_registration_call_sites_checked.site: lowerer_preseed_external_items_into_acc_mut (self-hosted/ir/lower.sio ~2924, inline registration inside the real multi-module 'external programs' loop)
all_registration_call_sites_checked.reliable_marker_result: FIRES 124 times for ArgList (once per external-program pass), always with the correct raw_field_count=2. This is the only site confirmed to observably and correctly see ArgList during the real compile.

all_registration_call_sites_checked.site: lowerer_preseed_external_struct_items_mut (self-hosted/ir/lower.sio ~2738, a THIRD, separate inline-registration function with its own explicit 'silently no-ops' workaround comment)
all_registration_call_sites_checked.reliable_marker_result: ZERO hits for ArgList with the reliable ir_name_eq check (despite an earlier, unreliable byte-comparison check also showing zero -- so this negative result is trustworthy).

all_registration_call_sites_checked.site: ir_fast_summary_register_struct_fields_owned (self-hosted/ir/lower.sio ~4010, a recursive, purely-functional/by-value struct-table builder, itself carrying an explicit comment about a nested-store by-value-aggregate miscompile already worked around)
all_registration_call_sites_checked.reliable_marker_result: ZERO hits for ArgList with the reliable ir_name_eq check.

all_registration_call_sites_checked.site: lowerer_preseed_program_items_mut (self-hosted/ir/lower.sio ~3634, uses a raw-pointer item cache (LOWER_PRESEED_ITEM_PTRS) rather than the standard linked-list walk; feeds the 'hot path' IrProgramSummary used by lower_program_bodies_from_summary_with_epistemic_boxed_owned)
all_registration_call_sites_checked.reliable_marker_result: ZERO hits for ArgList even AFTER fixing its call to the shared _direct_mut function into an inline registration (attempt 4) and placing the diagnostic print directly inside that new inline code.

all_registration_call_sites_checked.site: lowerer_lower_program_bodies_dedup_mut's ItemFn branch (the presumed body-lowering half of the real multi-module pipeline, called 124 times -- once per program, matching lowerer_preseed_external_items_into_acc_mut's own 124 firings)
all_registration_call_sites_checked.reliable_marker_result: ZERO hits for a marker checking name == 'arg_list_get' with ir_name_eq, across all 124 sessions. arg_list_get's body-lowering is confirmed to NOT happen via this function, despite it being structurally the most obvious candidate (paired 1:1 with the external-items preseed loop that DOES correctly see ArgList).

the_most_promising_unexplored_lead.summary: Use a gdb hardware watchpoint on the exact memory address of struct_layouts' ArgList entry (or, more robustly, of the whole StructLayoutTable Box) during a live invocation of gen1 performing the actual `build main.sio out.elf` self-compile, breaking on every WRITE to that memory region. This sidesteps the entire problem this session ran into -- guessing which of many candidate SOURCE functions is responsible -- by observing every write EMPIRICALLY, in the order it actually happens, with a full backtrace at each write. It was proposed to the user as an alternative during this session (declined in favor of stopping to document instead, given the time already spent) and remains the strongest concrete next step.
practical_notes: gen1 (or gen2, whichever binary is under test) is a native, stripped, hand-written ELF with NO section headers and NO debug symbols (readelf -S reports 'There are no sections in this file'). gdb can still watch/break on it live (breakpoints and watchpoints work on raw addresses of a running process), but static tools (objdump, addr2line) do not work at all -- everything must be done via a live, attached/run gdb session, as this whole investigation's gdb work already established.

The relevant table is (per self-hosted/ir/lower.sio's struct definitions) a 1024-entry array of up-to-128-field entries each -- large. A watchpoint on the WHOLE table may fire an enormous number of times (every struct's every field, across ~1552 modules). Narrowing to just the slot ArgList eventually occupies requires first letting registration happen once (to learn the address), or watching a smaller, more specific sub-region once the ArgList slot index is known from an earlier, unwatched run.

An easier variant: since the crash is now proven to be about arg_list_get's OWN compiled machine code specifically (not a live process's runtime data), and since gen1 compiling main.sio takes ~40-70 minutes to reach the point where arg_list_get gets lowered, a *conditional* watchpoint or breakpoint scoped to only fire once compilation reaches roughly that point (e.g. break at entry of whatever function is confirmed via `cur_fn=arg_list_get` diagnostic prints to be lowering it, THEN set the memory watchpoint from there) would cut the noise dramatically versus watching from process start.

Given every rebuild costs ~10-15 minutes for gen1 alone, doing this INTERACTIVELY inside a single already-running gen1 process (rather than rebuilding gen1 with new print instrumentation each time, as this whole session did) is much cheaper per iteration -- gdb can single-instance-attach to the long-running gen1 process performing the self-compile and set/adjust watchpoints without needing a rebuild at all, which is the main reason this technique should be tried before any further print-instrumentation cycles.

session_cost_note: This investigation, across the third-bug root-causing (documented in the two companion audit files) and this session's four fix attempts, consumed on the order of 20+ full gen1-rebuild-then-gen2-self-compile cycles, each costing roughly 15-90+ minutes (one cycle, attempt 3, took over 2 hours due to the performance regression it introduced). No code changes from this session were committed to the repository. This document and its two companions (already merged via PR #2408) are the only lasting artifacts.
